newsitem.title: USA: Key West defeated in fight for Hemingway fiesta.
newsitem.headline: Key West defeated in fight for Hemingway fiesta.

text.p: This Florida Keys island where Ernest Hemingway lived, wrote, drank and fished has been defeated by a posh resort where he never set foot in the fight to host an officially-sanctioned fiesta celebrating his life.
The Thursday announcement ended weeks of public wrangling and delicate talks over who should be awarded the lucrative marketing licence from the heirs of the late writer.

"The Hemingway sons don't want a rowdy beer crowd. They don't want the type of crowd that would attend a look-alike contest. They want an art and literary crowd," said Marla Metzner, the New York-based agent for the Hemingway sons.

Key West has held its own birthday bash for Hemingway each July since 1981. The events drew an estimated 10,000 people for 10 days of arm-wrestling matches, writing contests, and a boozy look-alike contest at the famed Sloppy Joe's Bar.

Last month the Hemingways threatened to sue the organisers of the Hemingway Days Festival if they did not relinquish control of the events and hand over 10 percent of the profits. Patrick Hemingway said his father was being portrayed as a hard-drinking slob.

Organiser Michael Walton called off the fiesta and talks on rescuing it broke off on Thursday when Metzner announced that Sanibel Island, an upscale resort community on Florida's west coast, would be chosen over Key West, where Hemingway lived from 1929 to 1940 and penned such classics as "To Have and Have Not" and "For Whom the Bell Tolls."

"Upper Michigan's Walloon Lake, Paris' Left Bank, Pamplona's perilous streets, Key West, Africa's green hills, Europes battlefields, Cuba's seacoast, Idaho's trout streams...all of these memorable locales could legitimately serve as an appropriate venue for Hemingway aficionados to gather in celebration of his life and work," Tom Kelly wrote in a commentary in Friday's Fort Lauderdale Sun Sentinel.
"But Sanibel island? An effete Key West wannabe...Say it isn't so Papa, he said, adding that Hemingway would not have been caught dead there.
The turning point in negotiations was a cocktail party where Metzner received an earful of criticism from prominent Key Westers.

"They said Ernest Hemingway would be no one without Key West. Several people actually felt the family should pay Key West a royalty for making Hemingway so well known. The family was not really receptive to that idea," Metzner said.
She said had reached a preliminary "handshake agreement with Sloppy Joe's to license the look-alike contest.
Hemingway's links to Sanibel are tenous. His niece Hilary lives there and his father once visited but there is no record Hemingway himself ever went there.
